title: The Spectrum of Register
text:
Register refers to the level of formality a speaker adopts according to context, audience and purpose. At one end of the spectrum lies the highly formal register, characterised by elaborate syntax, precise terminology and the absence of contractions. Legal documents and academic treatises exemplify this style, whereas casual conversation among intimates gravitates toward the colloquial end.

Yet the boundaries are rarely rigid, and skilled communicators shift between registers fluidly. A physician may explain a diagnosis with considerable technical rigour, then reassure a frightened patient with a more relaxed phrase. Such adaptability, rather than any single register, is often what distinguishes effective language use from merely correct language use.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what characterises the highly formal register?
options: Elaborate syntax, precise terminology and no contractions

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what example is given of shifting between registers?
options: A physician explaining a diagnosis technically, then reassuring a patient in a more relaxed way
A teacher grading essays in silence
A lawyer writing a text message to a friend
A novelist drafting a story in dialect

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of 'correct' language use?
options: Correctness alone does not guarantee effective communication
Formal language is always more effective than informal language
Register is irrelevant to effective communication

questions.text: What is the most likely purpose of the passage?
options: To argue that adapting register is a key communicative skill
To criticise legal and academic writing
To teach students how to avoid contractions
To describe the history of regional accents

vocabulary.definition: the level of formality used in a particular context
the ability to adjust to new conditions or situations

paragraph_translations: El registro se refiere al nivel de formalidad que adopta un hablante según el contexto, el público y el propósito. En un extremo del espectro se encuentra el registro altamente formal, caracterizado por una sintaxis elaborada, terminología precisa y la ausencia de contracciones. Los documentos legales y los tratados académicos ejemplifican este estilo, mientras que la conversación informal entre personas cercanas se inclina hacia el extremo coloquial.

Sin embargo, las fronteras rara vez son rígidas, y los comunicadores hábiles cambian de registro con fluidez. Un médico puede explicar un diagnóstico con considerable rigor técnico y luego tranquilizar a un paciente asustado con una frase más relajada. Esa adaptabilidad, más que cualquier registro en particular, es lo que suele distinguir el uso eficaz del idioma de un uso meramente correcto.
